outcome: Expression levels of immune cells (CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, NK, Treg, Th1, Th2, Th17 cells)
Levels of inflammatory cytokines secreted by immune cells (e.g., TNF-b)
cohort: The study included 21 preeclampsia-diagnosed pregnant women, 20 age-matched pregnant women without preeclampsia as controls, and 30 age-matched non-pregnant women as a reference group.
finding: The study found that preeclampsia patients exhibited reduced CD4+ and CD8+ cell numbers and downregulated Th1 cytokine levels (especially TNF-b) compared to controls, which authors suggest is a protective adaptive compensation mechanism to reduce maternal embryo rejection and the risk of premature delivery.
